title: The people ask for a king
summary: Mosiah seeks the people's will about who should be king. The people's response is that they want Aaron as king and ruler.

explicit_facts.text: Mosiah sends throughout the land to learn whom the people want as king.
The people's response is that they want Aaron as king and ruler.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Mosiah sends a message through the land to solicit the people's views.
unspecified_visual_details: The method used to solicit and collect the people's responses.
The appearance and number of people receiving or delivering the message.

spoken_dialogue.text: We are desirous that Aaron thy son should be our king and our ruler.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: the people

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Aaron as present; the passage says he had gone to the land of Nephi.

title: Mosiah sends a written word
summary: Aaron had gone to the land of Nephi, so Mosiah could not confer the kingdom on him. Aaron would not take the kingdom, and none of Mosiah's sons was willing to take it. Mosiah sent a written word among the people.

explicit_facts.text: Aaron had gone to the land of Nephi, so the king could not confer the kingdom on him.
Aaron would not take the kingdom, and none of Mosiah's sons was willing to take it.
King Mosiah again sent word among the people, in writing.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A written message may be shown without specifying its physical form.
unspecified_visual_details: The location and manner of distribution of the written word.
Whether a messenger or recipient is shown.

narration.text: Therefore king Mosiah sent again among the people;

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Aaron's absence and refusal are reported, not shown as events occurring alongside the sending of the written word.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show Aaron, Mosiah's other sons, or events in the land of Nephi as physically present in this scene.
Do not invent the contents of the written word.

title: Mosiah's written address begins
summary: In his written message, Mosiah asks the people to consider their desire for a king and explains that the person to whom the kingdom rightly belongs has declined it.

explicit_facts.text: Mosiah's written message addresses the people and asks them to consider their desire for a king.
Mosiah says the rightful heir has declined and will not take the kingdom.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The written address may be presented as off-screen speech over a setting supported by the message's distribution among the people.
unspecified_visual_details: The place where recipients read or hear the message.
The appearance of the written message.

narration.text: Behold, O ye my people, or my brethren,
he to whom the kingdom doth rightly belong has declined,

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Mosiah is the authorial speaker of the written address; the verses do not describe a live speech event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not stage this written address as a face-to-face gathering or depict Mosiah speaking to a crowd.

title: Mosiah warns of contention
summary: Mosiah warns that appointing another ruler could lead to contention, war, and bloodshed, and says the people have no right to destroy his son or another appointee.

explicit_facts.text: Mosiah fears appointing another ruler could cause contention and war if his son became angry and drew away part of the people.
Mosiah says the people have no right to destroy his son or another person appointed in his place.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The warning can be conveyed through off-screen narration over a neutral setting among the people.
unspecified_visual_details: Any actual conflict, combatants, weapons, or location of a possible war.

narration.text: there would rise contentions among you.
we have no right to destroy my son,

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The war and bloodshed are hypothetical warnings, not narrated events.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict an actual war, angry son, or attempt to destroy anyone.

title: A call to seek peace
summary: Mosiah warns that if his son returned to pride and claimed the kingdom, he and the people could commit sin. Mosiah urges the people to seek peace.

explicit_facts.text: Mosiah says that if his son returned to pride and claimed the kingdom, he and the people could commit much sin.
Mosiah urges the people to look ahead and do what will make for peace.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The written warning can be conveyed as off-screen narration.
unspecified_visual_details: The setting in which people receive the written message.

narration.text: let us be wise and look forward to these things,
do that which will make for the peace of this people.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The son reclaiming the kingdom is conditional, not a narrated event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the son reclaiming the kingdom or any resulting sin or conflict.

title: Mosiah proposes judges
summary: Mosiah says he will remain king for the rest of his life while proposing judges to judge according to law and God's commandments. He contrasts God's just judgments with the fallibility of human judgments.

explicit_facts.text: Mosiah says he will be king for the remainder of his days and proposes appointing wise judges to judge according to law and God's commandments.
Mosiah says God's judgments are always just, while human judgments are not always just.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Mosiah's proposal can be rendered as off-screen narration over a neutral setting.
unspecified_visual_details: The form of the proposed judges or the place where the message is read.

narration.text: I will be your king the remainder of my days;
the judgments of God are always just,

doctrinal_or_story_notes: This is a proposal in Mosiah's written message; the appointment of judges occurs later.
prohibited_inventions: Do not portray judges being appointed in this scene.

title: The possibility of just kings
summary: The speaker explains when kingship would be expedient and says he has labored to teach God's commandments and establish peace throughout the land.

explicit_facts.text: The speaker says that if just kings consistently established God's laws and judged according to his commandments, kingship would be expedient.
The speaker cites his father Benjamin as an example of such a king.
The speaker says he has labored to teach God's commandments and establish peace throughout the land.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The words can be presented without depicting the speaker or the past events he mentions.
unspecified_visual_details: The speaker's appearance and location.
How the words are visually presented.

narration.text: it would be expedient that ye should always have kings to rule over you.
to teach you the commandments of God, and to establish peace throughout the land,

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Benjamin is cited as a past example; the verses do not place him in the present scene.
The proposed just kings are hypothetical.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict hypothetical kings as reigning or show Benjamin physically present.
Do not turn the speaker's past labor into a new present-tense event.

title: Punishment and kings
summary: The speaker says he has punished those who committed iniquity according to the crime and the law, then argues against having a king or kings because not all men are just.

explicit_facts.text: The speaker says he has punished those who committed iniquity according to their crimes and the law given by their fathers.
The speaker says that because not all men are just, it is not expedient to have a king or kings rule over them.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The statements can be presented as text or off-screen narration without depicting a particular punishment.
unspecified_visual_details: The speaker's appearance and location.
The identity of any person punished or addressed.

narration.text: And whosoever has committed iniquity, him have I punished according to the crime which he has committed, according to the law which has been given to us by our fathers.
Now I say unto you, that because all men are not just it is not expedient that ye should have a king or kings to rule over you.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The punishment is reported retrospectively; do not stage it as a present event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent or depict a specific crime, offender, punishment, king, or setting.
Do not identify or visually depict the speaker or audience beyond what the verses state.

title: The warning of King Noah
summary: Mosiah warns how much iniquity and destruction one wicked king can cause, recalling King Noah and his people, who suffered destruction and bondage.

explicit_facts.text: Mosiah says one wicked king can cause much iniquity and great destruction.
Mosiah recalls King Noah and his people's wickedness, destruction, and bondage.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The warning may be shown as off-screen narration over the setting where the written message is received.
unspecified_visual_details: The appearance of King Noah, his people, or the historical events being recalled.

narration.text: how much iniquity doth one wicked king cause to be committed,
they were brought into bondage.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: King Noah and his people are mentioned in a recollection; the verses do not place them physically in the present scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict King Noah, his people, their destruction, or bondage as a present-tense event.

title: Deliverance from bondage
summary: Mosiah says the people would have remained in bondage without their Creator's intervention and sincere repentance. He says the Lord delivered them after they humbled themselves and cried to him.

explicit_facts.text: Mosiah says the people would have remained in bondage without their Creator's intervention and their sincere repentance.
Mosiah says the Lord delivered them from bondage because they humbled themselves and cried to him.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The message can be represented through off-screen narration without a literal depiction of divine intervention.
unspecified_visual_details: The historical setting and visible actions of the people during their repentance and deliverance.

narration.text: he did deliver them because they did humble themselves before him;
he did deliver them out of bondage;

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The Lord's deliverance is described in Mosiah's retrospective message; no visible appearance of the Lord is stated.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the Lord appearing or turn the past deliverance into a present event.

title: The dangers of an unrighteous king
summary: Mosiah warns that dethroning an iniquitous king requires much contention and bloodshed. He describes a king who keeps guards, rejects earlier laws and God's commandments, enacts wicked laws, and sends armies against rebels.

explicit_facts.text: The warning says an iniquitous king cannot be dethroned without much contention and bloodshed.
The king described has friends in iniquity, keeps guards, tears up laws of earlier righteous rulers, and tramples God's commandments.
The king described enacts laws, causes those who disobey them to be destroyed, and sends armies against rebels.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The warning could appear as text without depicting the described king or conflicts as events occurring now.
unspecified_visual_details: Mosiah's appearance and location.
The appearance of the described king, guards, people, and armies.

narration.text: ye cannot dethrone an iniquitous king save it be through much contention, and the shedding of much blood.
he keepeth his guards about him;
an unrighteous king doth pervert the ways of all righteousness.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The warning is attributable to Mosiah as part of his written message, not to an unnamed speaker.
The king's actions are described in the warning, not narrated as occurring in the present scene.
Trampling the commandments is figurative language, not a literal action to depict.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a particular king, rebellion, destruction, or war as occurring now.
Do not invent Mosiah's appearance or location.

title: Choose judges by the people's voice
summary: Mosiah says such abominations should not come upon the people and urges them to choose judges by the people's voice, according to the laws given by their fathers. He says the people's voice should govern their business.

explicit_facts.text: Mosiah says it is not expedient that the abominations of an unrighteous king come upon the people.
Mosiah urges the people to choose judges by their voice, according to the laws given by their fathers.
Mosiah says the people should do their business by the voice of the people.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The written instruction can be conveyed as off-screen narration.
unspecified_visual_details: The manner in which the people will choose judges.

narration.text: choose you by the voice of this people, judges,
to do your business by the voice of the people.

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the judges being chosen here; that happens later in the chapter.

title: Accountability of the people's choice
summary: The verses give a conditional warning about the people's choice and describe conditional procedures for judging judges.

explicit_facts.text: If the voice of the people chooses iniquity, the judgments of God will come upon them.
If judges do not judge according to the given law, they may be judged by a higher judge.
If higher judges do not judge righteously, a small number of lower judges may be gathered to judge them according to the voice of the people.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The conditional teaching may be presented without depicting any of its proposed events.
unspecified_visual_details: The setting and appearance of any speaker or listeners are not described.

narration.text: And if the time comes that the voice of the people doth choose iniquity,
ye can cause that they may be judged of a higher judge.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The warning and judicial procedures are conditional statements, not narrated events.
prohibited_inventions: Do not stage an election, divine destruction, a gathering of judges, or a trial as an event occurring in this scene.
Do not identify a speaker or depict a divine figure.

title: No king and shared responsibility
summary: Mosiah commands the people to have no king and says their sins will be their own responsibility. He desires an end to inequality and a land of liberty where people enjoy equal rights and privileges.

explicit_facts.text: Mosiah commands the people to have no king and says the people will answer for their own sins.
Mosiah says kings' iniquities have caused the sins of many people and are answered upon the kings.
Mosiah desires an end to inequality and a land of liberty where every person may enjoy equal rights and privileges.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The written message can be shown as off-screen narration.
unspecified_visual_details: The appearance of a future land of liberty or any specific representation of equality.

narration.text: that ye have no king;
I desire that this land be a land of liberty,

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a new constitution, symbol, or institution not specified in the verses.

title: Mosiah explains the burdens of kingship
summary: Mosiah writes further about a righteous king's trials, the people's murmuring, and the disadvantages of an unrighteous king, including wars, contentions, bloodshed, and other iniquities.

explicit_facts.text: Mosiah writes more, explaining the trials and troubles of a righteous king and the people's murmuring, and says every person should bear a part of the burden.
Mosiah explains the disadvantages of an unrighteous king, including wars, contentions, bloodshed, stealing, plundering, and other iniquities.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The extended written explanation can be represented as off-screen narration.
unspecified_visual_details: Any specific war, theft, plundering, or other crime in the historical examples.

narration.text: the burden should come upon all the people,
these things ought not to be,

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The listed evils are explanatory examples, not newly narrated events.
prohibited_inventions: Do not stage wars, crimes, or bloodshed as current events.

title: The people accept Mosiah's words
summary: After King Mosiah sends his words among the people, they are convinced of their truth. They relinquish their desire for a king, want every man to have an equal chance throughout the land, and express willingness to answer for their own sins.

explicit_facts.text: King Mosiah sent these things forth among the people, who were convinced of the truth of his words.
The people relinquished their desires for a king and became exceedingly anxious that every man should have an equal chance throughout the land.
Every man expressed a willingness to answer for his own sins.

unspecified_visual_details: Where and how the people's change of mind was expressed.
The people's appearance.

narration.text: Therefore they relinquished their desires for a king,

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict an assembly; it is not described in these verses.
Do not invent spoken responses, a voting procedure, or a visible appearance for Mosiah.

title: The people assemble to choose judges
summary: People assemble in groups throughout the land to cast their voices concerning who should be their judges. They rejoice in their liberty and esteem Mosiah.

explicit_facts.text: The people assemble in bodies throughout the land to cast their voices concerning who should be their judges according to the law given them.
The people rejoice because of the liberty granted to them.
The people esteem Mosiah greatly; he had not exacted riches or delighted in bloodshed, had established peace, and had granted that his people should be delivered from bondage.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Groups of people gathering in more than one part of the land can represent the assemblies.
unspecified_visual_details: The number, arrangement, clothing, and appearance of the people.
The specific locations of the assemblies.

narration.text: they were exceedingly rejoiced because of the liberty which had been granted unto them.
they did esteem him, yea, exceedingly, beyond measure.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Mosiah is discussed in verse 40, but his presence at an assembly is not stated.
prohibited_inventions: Do not identify the land as Zarahemla.
Do not depict Mosiah attending, campaigning, or speaking to an assembly.
Do not invent a voting procedure or spoken declarations.

title: Judges are appointed
summary: Judges are appointed throughout the land, and Alma is appointed the first chief judge. He judges righteously, there is continual peace through the land, and the reign of the judges begins.

explicit_facts.text: Judges are appointed throughout the land to judge according to the law.
Alma is appointed the first chief judge and is also the high priest. His father had conferred the office upon him and given him charge concerning the affairs of the church.
Alma walks in the ways of the Lord, keeps his commandments, and judges righteous judgments; there is continual peace through the land.
The reign of the judges begins throughout the land of Zarahemla among the Nephites, with Alma as the first and chief judge.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Alma and other judges may be shown as distinct figures during the transition to the reign of judges.
unspecified_visual_details: The appointment process, the identity of the other judges, and how appointments are formalized.

narration.text: And thus commenced the reign of the judges throughout all the land of Zarahemla

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The conferral by Alma's father is described as having already occurred; it is not part of the present appointment.
prohibited_inventions: Do not name Alma's father from outside these verses or depict the earlier conferral as occurring during the judges' appointment.
Do not invent appointment dialogue or ceremonies.

title: The end of the kings’ reign
summary: His father dies at eighty-two. Mosiah also dies at sixty-three, in the thirty-third year of his reign. The reign of kings over the people of Nephi and the days of Alma end.

explicit_facts.text: His father died at eighty-two, having lived to fulfill the commandments of God.
Mosiah died at sixty-three in the thirty-third year of his reign, five hundred and nine years after Lehi left Jerusalem.
The reign of kings over the people of Nephi ended.
The days of Alma, the founder of their church, ended.

unspecified_visual_details: The location and circumstances of either death.
The appearance of the people mentioned.
The referent of “his” in verse 45 is not identified within these verses.

narration.text: And thus ended the reign of the kings over the people of Nephi;

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verses report deaths and an ending, but do not establish Alma’s physical presence at either death.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Alma as present at either death.
Do not invent a deathbed, cause of death, ceremony, burial, or dialogue.
